hadiths.arab icText: عَنِ /94 ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ /94 ، /27 عَنْ /26 عَطَاءٍ /26 فِي /20 الشَّهْرَيْنِ يُتَدَارَكَانِ عَلِي الْمُسَافِرِ ، قَالَ : كَالْمَرِيضِ سَوَاءٌ
hadiths.english_translation: From Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' regarding the two months that catch up on the traveler, he said: Like the sick person, the same

narrators.name: ابن جريج
narrators.full_name: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Jurayj al-Makki
reliabilityIssues: Uses 'an which may indicate indirect transmission

chainIssues: Ibn Jurayj is known mudallis using 'an
Statement of Tabi'i (Ata'), not reaching Prophet ﷺ

plainChains: Ibn Jurayj -> Ata' ibn Abi Rabah

potential_issues.issue: Ibn Jurayj is a Category 3 mudallis according to Ibn Hajar's classification, using the indirect term 'an (عَنْ)
potential_issues.impact: While Ibn Jurayj is generally reliable, his tadlis when using 'an requires caution. However, since he's widely considered trustworthy, this doesn't severely impact the grade.

potential_issues.issue: This is a maqtu' narration (statement of Ata' al-Tabi'i), not attributed to the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: This is a legal opinion of Ata', not a prophetic hadith

Topics: Making up missed fasts while traveling
Comparison between traveler and sick person in fasting

hadiths.arabicText: عَنِ /94 ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ /94 ، قَالَ : /27 قُلْتُ /26 لِعَطَاءٍ /26 /20 فَرَجُلٌ أَفْطَرَ فِي رَمَضَانَ فِي سَفَرٍ...
hadiths.english_translation: From Ibn Jurayj, he said: I said to Ata': What about a man who broke fast in Ramadan while traveling, then remained traveling until another Ramadan reached him while traveling, what is between that? He said: Nothing is upon him except that he makes up the first one, and he does not have to feed. I said: What about a man who broke fast in Ramadan while traveling, then he resided and did not make it up until the next Ramadan reached him while traveling, can he break fast if he wishes? He said: Yes, then he feeds thirty poor people, thirty mudds

narrators.name: ابن جريج
narrators.full_name: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Jurayj al-Makki

chainIssues: This is Ibn Jurayj's direct questioning of Ata' (qultu), which is stronger than عَنْ
Statement of Tabi'i, not prophetic hadith

plainChains: Ibn Jurayj -> Ata' ibn Abi Rabah (direct questioning)

potential_issues.issue: This is a maqtu' narration (legal opinion of Ata'), not from the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: This represents Ata's fiqh opinion on making up Ramadan fasts

Topics: Delaying making up Ramadan fasts
Traveler who remains traveling between Ramadans
Fidyah (feeding) for delayed fasts

hadiths.arabicText: /27 عَنِ /94 الثَّوْرِيِّ /94 ، فِي /20 الرَّجُلِ يُفْطِرُ أَيَّامًا فِي سَفَرٍ ، ثُمَّ يَمُوتُ فِي سَفَرِهِ
hadiths.english_translation: From al-Thawri regarding the man who breaks fast for days while traveling, then dies during his travel, he said: Nothing is upon him. And this falls within the statement of Ibn Abbas, al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, Ata', and al-Zuhri

narrators.name: الثوري
narrators.full_name: Sufyan ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Thawri

chainIssues: Statement of al-Thawri (imam of fifth generation)

potential_issues.issue: This is al-Thawri's fiqh opinion, not a hadith chain
potential_issues.impact: Represents scholarly consensus among early authorities on this issue

Topics: Death while traveling before making up fasts
No obligation on deceased traveler to have fasts made up

hadiths.arabicText: عَنْ /94 مَعْمَرٍ /94 ، /27 عَنْ /26 قَتَادَةَ /26 ، فِي /20 رَجُلٍ يُفْطِرُ أَيَّامًا فِي سَفَرٍ
hadiths.english_translation: From Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding a man who breaks fast for days while traveling, then dies before he resides, he said: Food should be given on his behalf for each day to a poor person

narrators.name: قتادة
reliabilityIssues: However, this is his direct opinion, not reporting from others

chainIssues: Statement of Qatadah (Tabi'i), differing opinion from al-Thawri's view in previous narration

potential_issues.issue: Qatadah is a Category 3 mudallis, but here he's expressing his own opinion
potential_issues.impact: No impact as this is his fiqh opinion, not a narration requiring direct hearing

potential_issues.issue: This opinion contradicts the previous narration from al-Thawri
potential_issues.impact: Shows scholarly difference on whether fidyah is required for deceased traveler

Topics: Death while traveling before making up fasts
Fidyah for deceased who owed fasts
Scholarly differences on obligations of the deceased

hadiths.english_translation: From Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, he said regarding making up Ramadan: Fast it as you broke it

narrators.name: الزهري
narrators.full_name: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri
reliabilityIssues: mudallis (Category 3 per Ibn Hajar, though generally considered reliable even with 'an)

narrators.name: سالم
narrators.full_name: Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab

chainIssues: Al-Zuhri uses 'an and is known for tadlis (Category 3)
However, his narration from Salim is well-established

potential_issues.issue: Al-Zuhri is a Category 3 mudallis using the indirect term 'an (عَنْ)
potential_issues.impact: While al-Zuhri's tadlis should be noted, he is widely considered extremely reliable and his connection to Salim is well-established. This is mentioned but doesn't significantly downgrade the hadith.

Topics: Method of making up Ramadan fasts
Whether to fast consecutively or separately

hadiths.english_translation: From Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Shihab narrated to me, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, he said: Fast it as you broke it. And Urwah said: Aisha said: It was revealed: 'A number of other days consecutively,' then 'consecutively' was dropped

narrators.name: ابن جريج
narrators.full_name: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Jurayj al-Makki
reliabilityIssues: mudallis (Category 3), but uses explicit term حَدَّثَنِي here

narrators.name: ابن شهاب (الزهري)
narrators.full_name: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri

narrators.name: سالم
narrators.full_name: Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab

chainIssues: Ibn Jurayj uses explicit term حَدَّثَنِي, which solves tadlis issue
Also contains separate report from Aisha about Quranic verse

plainChains: Ibn Jurayj -> al-Zuhri (hadathani) -> Salim -> Ibn Umar

potential_issues.issue: Contains two separate reports: one from Ibn Umar (mawquf) and one from Aisha about Quranic revelation
potential_issues.impact: Both are companion-level reports with strong chains

Topics: Method of making up Ramadan fasts
Abrogation in Quranic verses about fasting

hadiths.english_translation: From al-Thawri, from Ubaydullah, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, he said: He makes it up consecutively

narrators.name: الثوري
narrators.full_name: Sufyan ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Thawri

chainIssues: This is the famous 'Golden Chain': Malik/Thawri -> Ubaydullah -> Nafi' -> Ibn Umar

potential_issues.issue: Multiple uses of 'an (عَنْ) throughout the chain
potential_issues.impact: However, all narrators are highly reliable (Thiqah Thabt) and this specific chain (via Nafi' from Ibn Umar) is one of the most authentic chains in hadith literature. The use of 'an by reliable non-mudallis narrators is generally acceptable.

potential_issues.issue: This opinion contradicts the previous report from Ibn Umar saying 'fast it as you broke it'
potential_issues.impact: Shows Ibn Umar may have had varying opinions, or this may represent different contexts

Topics: Making up Ramadan fasts consecutively

hadiths.english_translation: From al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, and from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, they both said: Consecutively

narrators.name: الثوري
narrators.full_name: Sufyan ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Thawri

chainIssues: Two separate chains converging on same opinion

narrators.name: الثوري
narrators.full_name: Sufyan ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Thawri

potential_issues.issue: These are opinions of Tabi'un (Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Sha'bi), not from Companions or Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: Represents fiqh opinions of early second generation scholars
All narrators are reliable and not known for tadlis, making 'an acceptable

Topics: Making up Ramadan fasts consecutively
Opinion of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Sha'bi

hadiths.english_translation: From al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, he said: Consecutively

narrators.name: الثوري
narrators.full_name: Sufyan ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Thawri

narrators.name: أبو إسحاق
narrators.full_name: Amr ibn Abdullah al-Sabi'i (Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i)
reliabilityIssues: Narrations from him by early students like al-Thawri are generally reliable

narrators.name: الحارث
reliabilityIssues: Considered weak (da'if) by majority of scholars
Accused of lying by some, though others considered him truthful but weak in memory

chainIssues: al-Harith al-A'war is a weak narrator
Abu Ishaq had ikhtilat but this is via al-Thawri (early student)

plainChains: al-Thawri -> Abu Ishaq -> al-Harith al-A'war -> Ali ibn Abi Talib

potential_issues.issue: al-Harith ibn Abdullah al-A'war is considered weak (da'if) by the majority of hadith scholars
potential_issues.impact: His presence in the chain weakens the narration significantly. He was accused by some of fabrication, though others considered him merely weak in memory.

potential_issues.issue: Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i had ikhtilat (confusion) in later life
potential_issues.impact: However, this narration comes through al-Thawri who was an early student of Abu Ishaq, so his narrations are generally considered reliable (before ikhtilat).

Topics: Making up Ramadan fasts consecutively
Opinion attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib

hadiths.english_translation: From al-Thawri, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Ibn al-Musayyib, he said: Consecutively

narrators.name: الثوري
narrators.full_name: Sufyan ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Thawri

plainChains: al-Thawri -> Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari -> Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib

potential_issues.issue: This is a maqtu' narration (opinion of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, a Tabi'i), not from a Companion or Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: Represents the fiqh opinion of one of the most prominent Tabi'un
However, all are highly reliable (Thiqah Thabt) and not known for tadlis, so 'an is acceptable

Topics: Making up Ramadan fasts consecutively
Opinion of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib
